title: Hepatitis B and C Screening Coverage among High-risk Populations in Saudi Arabia: A National Analysis of Surveillance Data and Alignment with the World Health Organization Viral Hepatitis Elimination Targets (2016–2023)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Viral hepatitis B and C represent major global public health challenges, collectively responsible for approximately 1.1 million deaths annually. The study aimed to address the lack of comprehensive analyses on screening coverage among high-risk populations in Saudi Arabia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional descriptive study analyzed secondary data from the WHO Global Health Observatory estimates, Saudi Ministry of Health surveillance reports, and published epidemiological surveys (2016–2023). The study focused on high-risk populations such as healthcare workers, blood donors, prisoners, hemodialysis patients, and pregnant women.
analysis.methods: Descriptive statistics, including 95% confidence intervals (CIs), characterized coverage patterns by population group, geographic region, and temporal trends. Comparative analysis assessed alignment with the WHO GHSS targets.
analysis.main_results: Overall hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing coverage among high-risk populations reached 74.3% (95% CI: 74.2–74.4) in 2023, while anti-hepatitis C virus (HCV) testing coverage reached 68.9% (95% CI: 68.8–69.0). Blood donor screening achieved near-universal coverage (99.8%, 95% CI: 99.79–99.81, for both HBsAg and anti-HCV). Healthcare worker screening demonstrated 81.4% (95% CI: 81.3–81.5) HBsAg and 76.2% (95% CI: 76.0–76.4) anti-HCV coverage. Hemodialysis patient screening reached 94.7% (95% CI: 94.4–95.0) for HBsAg. Antenatal screening for HBsAg achieved 89.3% (95% CI: 89.2–89.4) nationally. However, prisoner screening remained lowest at 41.2% (95% CI: 40.8–41.6) for HBsAg and 38.7% (95% CI: 38.4–39.0) for anti-HCV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Saudi Arabia has achieved strong screening coverage in clinical high-risk groups, but critical gaps persist among incarcerated populations and in border regions. This study provides a national analysis of screening coverage aligned with WHO elimination targets, highlighting the need for targeted interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted expansion of screening programs, integration with primary health care, and strengthened linkage to care to achieve the WHO 2030 viral hepatitis elimination targets. They also highlight the importance of addressing regional disparities and improving screening among vulnerable populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on secondary data and does not include direct measurements or interventions. The evidence strength is moderate, as the results are derived from descriptive statistics and comparative analysis of existing reports.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed hepatitis B and C screening coverage among high-risk populations in Saudi Arabia from 2016 to 2023, using secondary data from WHO and national surveillance reports. It found that overall HBsAg testing coverage reached 74.3% in 2023, while anti-HCV coverage was 68.9%. Blood donor screening was near-universal, while prisoner screening remained low at 41.2% for HBsAg and 38.7% for anti-HCV. Regional disparities were noted, with border regions lagging by 15–22 percentage points. The study highlights the need for targeted interventions to improve screening in vulnerable groups and align with WHO elimination targets. The evidence is moderate due to reliance on secondary data and descriptive analysis.

title: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen and Hepatitis D Antibody Positivity among Inmates of Jos Correctional Centre, Plateau State, Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) share transmission pathways, and ongoing HDV replication requires HBV surface antigen. Evidence from correctional facilities in Nigeria remains limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study assessed hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HDV antibody positivity among inmates of Jos Correctional Centre. HBsAg was detected in 43 of 235 participants (18.3%; 95% CI: 13.9–23.7%).
analysis.methods: In a cross-sectional serological survey, plasma samples from 235 incarcerated participants were tested for HBsAg using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). HBsAg-reactive samples were subsequently tested for anti-HDV antibodies by ELISA. Descriptive frequencies and Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated; Fisher’s exact test was used for selected sex- and exposure-stratified HBsAg comparisons.
analysis.main_results: Five of the 43 HBsAg-positive participants were anti-HDV positive (11.6%; 95% CI: 5.1–24.5%). HBsAg positivity was 42/227 (18.5%) among men and 1/8 (12.5%) among women (Fisher’s exact p = 1.00). Anti-HDV positivity occurred in five men and no women; only one HBsAg-positive woman was screened for anti-HDV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HBsAg and anti-HDV antibody positivity were observed in this correctional population. Anti-HDV positivity alone does not establish active HDV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support access to HBV screening, vaccination of susceptible individuals, HDV testing after HBsAg detection, and linkage to clinical assessment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Small subgroup counts precluded reliable risk-factor inference. The evidence is moderate as the study is limited by its cross-sectional design and small sample size.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a cross-sectional serological survey at Jos Correctional Centre in Nigeria to assess hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HDV antibody positivity among inmates. HBsAg was detected in 18.3% of participants, with 11.6% of HBsAg-positive individuals also showing anti-HDV positivity. The study found no anti-HDV positivity among women, highlighting potential gender disparities in HDV infection. The findings emphasize the importance of HBV screening and HDV testing in correctional settings, supporting targeted public health interventions. However, the study's small subgroup sizes limit the reliability of risk-factor inference, and the evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and limited sample size.

title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver and antiviral response in chronic hepatitis B: A systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aims to evaluate the impact of MAFLD on antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The central question is whether MAFLD influences virological, biochemical, and clinical responses to antiviral therapy in CHB.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA guidelines. The evidence base included studies from PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science, published up to November 30, 2025. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MAFLD was associated with lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, particularly among patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and increased odds of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy. However, no significant association was observed between MAFLD and hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance at any time-point.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Subgroup analyses suggested that antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach partly explained the heterogeneity in the overall findings, particularly for hepatitis B virus DNA clearance and HCC. The evidence does not report on the specific mechanisms linking MAFLD to these outcomes or the impact of MAFLD on other clinical outcomes such as liver fibrosis progression.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support the integration of metabolic risk assessment in the management of CHB and highlight the need for standardized definitions of MAFLD and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the association between metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The review included 32 studies, with 20 evaluating treatment efficacy and 13 assessing clinical outcomes. MAFLD was linked to lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, and increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy. However, no significant association was found with hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance. Subgroup analyses revealed heterogeneity in outcomes based on antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach. The study underscores the importance of metabolic risk assessment in CHB management and calls for standardized definitions of MAFLD.

title: Negatively Impacting Factors Against Effective Hepatitis B Vaccination

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the factors that negatively impact the effectiveness of hepatitis B vaccination. The central question is to identify the barriers that hinder the uptake of hepatitis B vaccines and to explore how these factors influence vaccination outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review was conducted using the Google Scholar search engine to gather published studies on the factors that hamper successful hepatitis B vaccination. A total of 26 journal articles were studied, with the most relevant items from the last 10 years being identified and analyzed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identified 18 barriers that hinder the effective uptake of hepatitis B vaccines. Lack of awareness and knowledge about Hepatitis B vaccination was the highest factor, cited in 69% (18) of the studies. Inadequate education among parents was mentioned in 41% (11) of the studies, while superstition and false perceptions about vaccination were noted in 36% (9) of the studies. The price and unavailability of the vaccine were mentioned in 27% (7) of the reviewed articles. The review also highlights that issues differ by region.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the barriers to effective hepatitis B vaccination vary significantly across regions, indicating a lack of uniformity in the challenges faced. There is no explicit mention of specific regions or populations where these barriers are most prevalent, which represents an evidence gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for an appropriately planned and well-organized hepatitis B vaccination policy to ensure adequate vaccine coverage. It suggests that addressing the identified barriers, such as improving awareness and education, is crucial for eradicating the hepatitis B virus.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the factors that negatively impact the effectiveness of hepatitis B vaccination. It identifies 18 barriers, with lack of awareness and knowledge being the most significant. The review highlights the importance of addressing these barriers through targeted policies and education to improve vaccine coverage and ultimately eradicate the virus. The findings suggest that regional differences in these challenges exist, indicating a need for localized strategies. The review was conducted using Google Scholar and included 26 journal articles from the last decade, emphasizing the necessity of well-organized vaccination programs.

title: Discovery of XT1061, a HBV Capsid Assembly Modulator, as a Promising Therapeutic Candidate for Clinical Treatment of HBV Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for effective therapeutic candidates for chronic HBV infection, given the limitations of current treatments which do not achieve functional cure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved the discovery and evaluation of compound XT1061 in vitro and in a murine AAV/HBV model.
analysis.methods: XT1061 was identified through structural optimization of GLP-26 and tested for anti-HBV activity in vitro and in vivo.
analysis.main_results: XT1061 exhibited potent anti-HBV activity in vitro (EC50 = 1.0 ± 0.1 nM) and induced rapid reduction of HBV DNA in the murine AAV/HBV model, with sustained viral DNA clearance throughout treatment. Combination therapy with XT1061 and pradefovir mesylate showed significantly enhanced efficacy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that XT1061 represents a promising therapeutic candidate for chronic HBV infection, with potential to facilitate functional cure when combined with other treatments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that XT1061 could provide a viable strategy for the clinical management of chronic HBV infection, potentially leading to functional cure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its preclinical nature and the need for further evaluation in larger, more diverse populations. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of human clinical trial data.

analysis.summary_en: This study discovered compound XT1061, a potent HBV capsid assembly modulator, which showed promising results in reducing HBV DNA in a murine model and in combination therapy with pradefovir mesylate. The findings suggest a potential new therapeutic strategy for chronic HBV infection.

title: Hepatitis B and C infections and risk of age related macular degeneration in a nationwide Korean cohort

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are associated with the subsequent development of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in a nationwide Korean cohort. Abstract Evidence on viral hepatitis and AMD remains limited, particularly from long-term prospective studies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide cohort study was conducted using National Health Insurance Service data, including 12,386,563 adults aged ≥ 40 years who underwent health examinations in 2009–2010 and were followed through 2023. During follow-up, 388,652 participants developed incident AMD.
analysis.methods: HBV and HCV infections were identified using diagnostic codes. Incident AMD was classified as exudative using Rare Intractable Disease registration codes and as nonexudative using Korean Classification of Diseases codes. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations.
analysis.main_results: In multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, HBV infection was associated with increased risks of exudative AMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05–1.32) and nonexudative AMD (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.60–1.76). title: Chronic Hepatitis B and Steatotic Liver Disease: From Bidirectional Interaction to Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and steatotic liver disease (SLD) are among the most prevalent chronic liver diseases worldwide and increasingly coexist, particularly in regions where hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains endemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examined the association between hepatic steatosis and virological markers in patients with chronic hepatitis B, using data from various diagnostic methods including liver biopsy, ultrasound, and controlled attenuation parameter (CAP).
analysis.methods: The study analyzed data from multiple sources using liver biopsy, ultrasound, and controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) to assess hepatic steatosis, and correlated these findings with virological markers such as serum HBV DNA, quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), and hepatitis B envelope antigen (HBeAg).
analysis.main_results: Reported prevalence of hepatic steatosis in CHB varies widely, reflecting the diagnostic modality and population studied rather than a single underlying figure.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These virological associations do not consistently predict long-term liver outcomes, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists after HBsAg seroclearance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Hepatic steatosis, metabolic dysfunction, steatohepatitis and fibrosis should therefore be assessed as distinct prognostic variables rather than as a single entity, with implications for HCC risk stratification and surveillance in CHB.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Studies using hepatic steatosis as the exposure report inconsistent findings for HCC, with adjusted estimates ranging from inverse to strongly positive.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and steatotic liver disease (SLD), highlighting their coexistence in endemic regions. It reports that the prevalence of hepatic steatosis in CHB varies depending on diagnostic methods, and that steatosis is more consistently linked to host metabolic and genetic factors than viral replication markers. The findings indicate that virological associations with steatosis do not reliably predict long-term liver outcomes, and HCC risk remains even after HBsAg seroclearance. The study suggests that hepatic steatosis, metabolic dysfunction, steatohepatitis, and fibrosis should be considered as separate prognostic variables for HCC risk assessment in CHB patients. However, the study notes that findings on HCC risk associated with steatosis are inconsistent, with adjusted estimates ranging from inverse to strongly positive. The evidence is moderate, as the study relies on observational data and does not provide definitive causal conclusions.

title: Prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) in Cte dIvoire

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d'Ivoire, HDV is not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021 at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d'Ivoire (CNTSCI). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and the mean age was 37 ± 9 years.
analysis.methods: HDV RNA was detected by nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888-1122 and 313-485). HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%).
analysis.main_results: Among the 43 donors with available HBV DNA results, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity of 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data, not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of HDV screening in individuals with chronic HBV infection, particularly in settings where viral load data is available, and suggest the need for further research to better understand HDV prevalence and its implications for public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single study with limited generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg-positive blood donors in Côte d'Ivoire using nested RT-PCR. It found that 90.7% of donors with available HBV DNA results had HDV RNA positivity, with 100% positivity in those with undetectable HBV viral load. The study highlights the need for systematic HDV screening in individuals with chronic HBV infection, particularly in follow-up care settings. However, the findings are hypothesis-generating due to the convenience sample and limited generalizability, indicating moderate evidence strength.

title: Pegylated interferon α-2b add-on to nucleos(t)ide analogues reduces hepatocellular carcinoma and decompensation in advanced fibrotic chronic hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the long-term prognosis benefit of add-on Peg-IFNα-2b therapy in patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. The current therapeutic strategy of adding pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) is primarily aimed at achieving functional cure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients diagnosed with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. Participants were divided into two groups: (1) Those receiving combination therapy (Peg-IFNα-2b add-on to ongoing NA treatment); and (2) Those receiving NA monotherapy.
analysis.methods: A 1:1 propensity score matching approach was applied to balance baseline characteristics between groups. In survival analysis, the outcomes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and decompensated cirrhosis were stratified by baseline clinical features and established HCC risk scores.
analysis.main_results: The analysis included 302 matched pairs, with a median follow-up duration of 220 weeks. Combination therapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of developing HCC (hazard ratio = 0.22; 95%CI: 0.11-0.48) and decompensated cirrhosis (hazard ratio = 0.39; 95%CI: 0.20-0.77) than NA monotherapy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These benefits were particularly pronounced among patients classified as intermediate-to-high risk by validated HCC prediction models and in those with persistent biochemical abnormalities lasting > 12 months. Add-on therapy with Peg-IFNα-2b to NAs is significantly associated with reduced HCC and decompensation in high-risk patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, supporting its use in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that combination therapy with Peg-IFNα-2b may offer important benefits for reducing HCC and decompensation in high-risk HBV patients. This could inform future treatment strategies for managing advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis in chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a retrospective cohort study, which may introduce bias and confounding factors. The evidence is moderate as it relies on propensity score matching and stratified survival analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the long-term prognosis benefit of add-on Peg-IFNα-2b therapy in patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. A retrospective cohort study design was used, with patients divided into combination therapy and NA monotherapy groups. Propensity score matching was applied to balance baseline characteristics, and survival analysis was stratified by clinical features and HCC risk scores. The results showed that combination therapy significantly reduced the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and decompensated cirrhosis compared to monotherapy, with hazard ratios of 0.22 (95%CI: 0.11-0.48) and 0.39 (95%CI: 0.20-0.77), respectively. These benefits were most evident in intermediate-to-high risk patients and those with persistent biochemical abnormalities. The findings support the use of Peg-IFNα-2b add-on therapy in high-risk HBV patients, potentially informing future treatment strategies. However, the study's retrospective nature introduces limitations, and the evidence is moderate due to reliance on matching and stratified analysis.

title: Association of IL-10 (rs1800896) Gene Polymorphism and Serum IL-10 Levels with Chronic Hepatitis B Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the correlation between IL-10 gene polymorphisms and the development of chronic hepatitis B infection, addressing the scientific problem of understanding immunogenetic factors influencing HBV infection progression.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective case control study was conducted involving 64 chronic HBV infections, 39 HBV clearance groups and 31 controls.
analysis.methods: The study used "Tetra-primer ARMS-PCR" to analyze single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) at IL10 promoter (-1082A>G; rs1800896) and Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) to determine IL-10 levels in patients with chronic HBV infections, HBV clearance and control group.
analysis.main_results: Based on allele polymorphism analysis, three genotypes were identified: AA (46.8 %), AG (43.7 %) and GG (9.3 %). The level of IL10 in HBV patients was significantly greater than that in other sets.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings indicate that polymorphism may not affect initial infection but rather disease progression or disease immune response.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future studies on the role of IL-10 polymorphisms in disease progression and immune response, potentially contributing to improved surveillance and targeted therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, but the evidence is supported by direct analysis of IL-10 polymorphisms and serum levels in defined groups, providing a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between IL-10 gene polymorphisms and chronic hepatitis B infection. It conducted a retrospective case control study involving 64 chronic HBV infections, 39 HBV clearance groups, and 31 controls. The methods included Tetra-primer ARMS-PCR for SNP analysis and ELISA for measuring IL-10 levels. Results showed three genotypes (AA, AG, GG) with varying frequencies, and significantly higher IL-10 levels in HBV patients compared to other groups. The authors interpreted these findings as suggesting that IL-10 polymorphisms may influence disease progression rather than initial infection. The study's results may contribute to understanding the immune response in chronic HBV infection and inform future research on targeted therapies. However, the retrospective design and potential for selection bias limit the confidence in the findings, which are considered to have moderate strength.

title: Translational Multiplexed Raman Pathological Imaging for Precise Diagnosis of HBV-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to address the lack of fully standardized workflows for routine clinical histopathology by developing a clinically applicable methodology for precise diagnosis of HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reported a clinically applicable methodology using monodisperse triple-bond Raman polymer nanoparticles (∼50 nm) to achieve high-performance multiplexed Raman imaging of 5 protein markers in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues.
analysis.methods: The technique integrates one-step labeling and single-scan acquisition to simultaneously evaluate viral etiology, tumor progression, and metastatic potential, effectively reducing misclassification risk in patients with discordant viral and oncogenic profiles, and completes the entire assay within approximately 24 h.
analysis.main_results: The method targets hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated HCC, combining the viral protein HBx with 4 clinically used indicators: AFP, GS, GPC3, and CD34. It further reveals a clinically critical dissociation: several high-grade HBV-HCC specimens exhibit markedly elevated oncogenic markers with comparatively low HBx expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that this approach enables high-fidelity spatial mapping and quantitative analysis by leveraging ultranarrow, well-resolved signals generated by triple-bond tags within the biological silent region (1800−2800 cm−1), which is a novel integration of pathogen identification and comprehensive cancer characterization.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings demonstrate substantial value for both cancer research and clinical diagnostics, particularly in improving the accuracy of diagnosis for HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the methodology's effectiveness in routine clinical settings has not been fully validated, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel methodology for the precise diagnosis of HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma using monodisperse triple-bond Raman polymer nanoparticles. The approach integrates one-step labeling and single-scan acquisition to simultaneously evaluate viral etiology, tumor progression, and metastatic potential, reducing misclassification risk in patients with discordant viral and oncogenic profiles. The method targets HBV-associated HCC by combining the viral protein HBx with 4 clinically used indicators: AFP, GS, GPC3, and CD34. It reveals a clinically critical dissociation where high-grade HBV-HCC specimens show elevated oncogenic markers with low HBx expression, consistent with antiviral therapy suppressing viral protein production without reversing tumor aggressiveness. The technique leverages ultranarrow, well-resolved signals in the biological silent region (1800−2800 cm−1) for high-fidelity spatial mapping and quantitative analysis. The study establishes a rapid and reliable histopathological platform with substantial value for cancer research and clinical diagnostics, though its effectiveness in routine settings remains to be validated, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Metabolomics reveals metabolite profiles associated with clinical cure of chronic HBV infection under different drug interventions

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify differential metabolites associated with complete cure in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with various regimens of entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, case-control study was conducted at the Mudan People's Hospital of Heze, Shandong, China, involving samples from hepatitis B virus patients enrolled between June 2, 2021, and December 30, 2023. Patients were grouped based on the treatment protocol and the evidence of complete cure.
analysis.methods: Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and metabolomics databases were used to identify differential metabolites and networks indicative of clinical cure. Data was analysed using the R language Ropls package.
analysis.main_results: Of the 50 patients, 13(26%) each were in Group A and Group B, while 12(24%) each were in Group E and Group W. A total of 52 differential metabolites showing altered abundance in Group A compared with the other groups were identified. The fold-change values were 1.28 for 9,10-DHOME, 1.12 for 12,13-DHOME and 1.33 for kaempferide, and guanidoacetic acid ranked first among the differential metabolites in Group A versus Group B (fold-change: 1.27, p=2.56×10-8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Kaempferide, 9,10-dihydroxy-12Z-octadecenoic acid and 12,13-dihydroxy-9Z-octadecenoic acid were common differential metabolites, indicating potential significance for achieving clinical cure in chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of biomarkers for monitoring treatment response and predicting clinical cure in chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a retrospective case-control study with a relatively small sample size, which may limit the generalisability of the results. The evidence is moderate as it is based on metabolomics analysis and statistical comparisons.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify differential metabolites associated with clinical cure in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with entecavir and pegylated interferon-alpha. Conducted at Mudan People's Hospital in China, it involved a retrospective case-control design with patients grouped based on treatment and cure status. Metabolomics techniques were used to detect altered metabolites, revealing 52 differential metabolites in cured patients compared to non-cured and untreated groups. Kaempferide and other metabolites showed significant fold-change values, suggesting their potential role in clinical cure. The results may help develop biomarkers for treatment monitoring. However, the study's retrospective nature and small sample size limit its generalisability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Pilot Model for Newly Diagnosed in-Hospital Bacterial and Fungal Infections in Decompensated Hepatitis B Cirrhosis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Recognizing infection risk during hospitalization is important in decompensated cirrhosis, although routine measurements may reflect infection already developing.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-center retrospective cohort included 150 patients admitted in 2023–2025. Complete-case analysis included 148 patients and 20 events.
analysis.methods: Admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score (MELD) were fixed as predictors for the primary Firth/Jeffreys penalized logistic model. We refitted the fixed model in 1000 bootstrap samples, assessed calibration and discrimination, and examined early-event exclusions and an admission-only ridge model. The hospital-recorded procedure variable was excluded from prediction.
analysis.main_results: Among 148 modeled patients, the NLR and MELD odds ratios were 1.073 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.025–1.124) and 1.062 (95% CI, 1.002–1.125). Apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.716 versus 0.633 for MELD alone. AUCs after separate exclusions of infections recorded by hospital day 2 or day 3 were 0.750 and 0.731, respectively. Fine–Gray subdistribution hazard ratios were 1.069 (95% CI 1.042–1.098) for NLR and 1.064 (1.021–1.109) for MELD.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This admission model showed modest discrimination with imprecise calibration.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Prospective external validation at a defined prediction time and horizon is needed before the model guides surveillance or treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Retrospective ascertainment and limited validation preclude clinical use.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a pilot model for predicting newly diagnosed in-hospital bacterial or fungal infections in patients with decompensated hepatitis B virus-related cirrhosis. A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from 150 patients admitted between 2023 and 2025. The model incorporated admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) scores as predictors. Results showed modest discrimination with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.716, and imprecise calibration. The study concluded that the model requires prospective external validation before it can be used in clinical practice. The findings suggest that further research is needed to improve the model's accuracy and applicability for surveillance and treatment decisions in patients with HBV-related cirrhosis.

title: Epidemiology of Hepatitis B and C Viral Infections Among Tuberculosis Patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limited evidence on the burden and clinical implications of hepatitis B and C infections among tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria. The research was needed due to the potential vulnerability of tuberculosis patients coinfected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV) to liver injury during treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Ebonyi State, Nigeria, among tuberculosis patients to assess the epidemiology of hepatitis B and C viral infections. It included specific objectives to determine the prevalence of HBV, HCV, and co-infection, as well as to identify risk factors and evaluate knowledge, attitude, and practices (KAP) of TB patients towards these infections.
analysis.methods: The study assessed HBV/HCV prevalence, risk factors, and patients’ knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP). It focused on tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria, and included general methods to evaluate the epidemiology of these infections.
analysis.main_results: It directly observed the prevalence of hepatitis B and C infections among tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the need for integrated management of tuberculosis and viral hepatitis infections. The study's novelty lies in its focus on the epidemiology of HBV and HCV among TB patients in Ebonyi State.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for integrated management of tuberculosis and viral hepatitis infections in Ebonyi State, Nigeria. They emphasize the importance of addressing co-infections to prevent liver injury during treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its abstract-only evidence, which may not capture detailed methodologies or outcomes. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of comprehensive data and the focus on general observations.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the limited evidence on the burden and clinical implications of hepatitis B and C infections among tuberculosis patients in Ebonyi State, Nigeria. It aimed to assess the epidemiology of these infections, including prevalence, risk factors, and knowledge, attitude, and practices (KAP) of TB patients. The research highlights the vulnerability of co-infected patients to liver injury during treatment and underscores the need for integrated management strategies. The findings suggest that addressing HBV and HCV co-infections is crucial for public health in the region. However, the study is limited by its abstract-only evidence, which restricts the depth of analysis and the strength of conclusions.

title: Immune Response to Hepatitis B Vaccination According to National EPI Schedule among Children Below 2 Years

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus infection is a public health burden globally. There is no comprehensive data regarding the immune response of the HBV vaccine at one year in our country.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted at EPI outdoor of Chittagong Medical College Hospital from January to December, 2022. Blood sample from 375 vaccinated children were tested for Anti-HBs titre by ELISA technique in between 9 months to 15 months.
analysis.methods: Statistical analyses were performed with Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 23.0.
analysis.main_results: This study shows that older children and male tend to have better immune responses after vaccination and malnutrition is a significant risk factor for low antibody titers. This study also shows that 79.2% of children had satisfactory or high levels of anti-HBs antibodies (≥10 mIU/mL). However, 20.8% of children had low antibody titers ( <10 mIU/mL) indicating inadequate immune protection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Most children vaccinated under the current EPI schedule develop protective immunity against hepatitis B; a small proportion remain vulnerable due to inadequate seroconversion.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted vaccination strategies and highlight the need for nutritional interventions to improve immune response in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and potential confounding factors. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single study with a specific population.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immune response to the Hepatitis B vaccine among children below 2 years of age in Bangladesh, focusing on the National EPI schedule. It highlights that older children and males tend to have better immune responses, while malnutrition is a significant risk factor for low antibody titers. The study found that 79.2% of children had satisfactory or high levels of anti-HBs antibodies, whereas 20.8% had inadequate immune protection. These results suggest that the current vaccination schedule is effective for most children but may require additional interventions for those at risk. The study's cross-sectional design and potential confounding factors limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

title: Intrinsic replication advantage of a Hepatitis B Virus genotype C strain is independent of the basal core promoter A1762T/G1764A mutation

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to isolate and characterize individual hepatitis B virus (HBV) strains from a patient co-infected with genotype B and C, and to directly compare their intrinsic replication capacities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: HBV DNA was isolated from a chronic hepatitis B patient. Two clones representing subgenotype B2 (c17) and C1 (c21) were selected, sequenced and transfected into HepG2 cells.
analysis.methods: Genotypes were determined by genotype-specific polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and full-length genomes were cloned. Viral replication was assessed via Southern blot and quantitative PCR. The role of the common A1762T/G1764A mutation in the C1 clone was investigated by site-directed mutagenesis.
analysis.main_results: The genotype C1 clone exhibited significantly higher replication capacity than the B2 clone. Counterintuitively, reverting the A1762T/G1764A mutation in the C1 clone to wild-type further enhanced its replication.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides a virological explanation for the association of HBV genotype C1 with severe disease outcomes in co-infection, showing that its replication advantage is independent of the classic basal core promoter mutation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the understanding of HBV genotype-specific replication dynamics and may contribute to improved surveillance and targeted therapeutic strategies for genotype C1 infections.

The researchers isolated and characterized HBV strains, cloned full-length genomes, and performed replication assays in HepG2 cells. The results suggest that genotype C1's association with severe disease outcomes in co-infection may be due to its inherent replication properties rather than the BCP mutation. The study provides insights into genotype-specific replication dynamics, which could inform future research and targeted therapeutic strategies. However, the findings are based on a single patient's strains and may not be generalizable to broader populations.

title: Autophagy-related gene expression is associated with fibrosis severity in chronic hepatitis B and fatty liver disease

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the transcriptional correlates of autophagy in human liver fibrosis, as autophagy's role in hepatocyte survival, stellate cell activation and inflammation is well established, yet its relationship with fibrosis severity remains poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed liver biopsy transcriptomes from 124 patients with chronic hepatitis B, identifying 20 autophagy-related genes that differed nominally between fibrotic and non-fibrotic tissue. It also examined two independent cohorts with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
analysis.methods: The researchers performed co-expression network analysis to prioritize genes, and an exploratory 15-gene neural-network classifier was developed and validated using bootstrap methods.
analysis.main_results: The classifier had an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.982, but bootstrap validation of a re-implemented development procedure gave an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.865. In whole blood from six healthy individuals and six with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis, the classifier had an AUC of 0.833 (95% confidence interval, 0.556–1.000).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that CCL2, CAPN2, and CDKN1A may serve as potential markers for fibrosis severity, although their cellular sources and roles in fibrosis remain unclear.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These genes could inform future research on fibrosis severity markers, potentially aiding in the development of diagnostic tools for liver diseases associated with hepatitis B.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its use of an exploratory classifier and the small sample size of healthy individuals and those with cirrhosis, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the association between autophagy-related gene expression and fibrosis severity in chronic hepatitis B and fatty liver disease. The researchers analyzed liver biopsy transcriptomes from 124 patients with chronic hepatitis B, identifying 20 autophagy-related genes that differed between fibrotic and non-fibrotic tissue. Co-expression network analysis highlighted CCL2, MYC, CDKN1A, and CAPN2, with their expression correlated with immune cell signatures and fibrosis stage after adjusting for inflammation grade, age, and sex. An exploratory 15-gene neural-network classifier showed an apparent AUC of 0.982, but bootstrap validation reduced this to 0.865, and the classifier had an AUC of 0.833 (95% confidence interval, 0.556–1.000) in whole blood from six healthy individuals and six with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis. The study suggests that these genes may serve as potential markers for fibrosis severity, though their cellular sources and roles in fibrosis are not yet known. The findings are of moderate significance for future research on fibrosis markers, but the study's limitations include its exploratory nature and small sample size.

title: Peripheral Blood Natural Killer Cell Quantity, Phenotype, and Function Across the Clinical Spectrum of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection: A Scoping Review

analysis.research_question_and_background: This scoping review aims to systematically map and critically examine the available evidence on the quantity, phenotype, and function of peripheral blood natural killer (NK) cells across the clinical spectrum of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including chronic HBV infection and hepatitis, HBV-related liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, and HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.study_design_and_population: Differences in clinical populations, disease classification, antiviral treatment, blood sample processing, flow cytometric gating strategies, measurement denominators, and functional assay conditions may limit direct comparisons between studies.
analysis.methods: The review will be guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), with additional attention to transparent reporting of literature searches using PRISMA-S.
analysis.main_results: Studies involving mixed HCC etiologies will be considered for HBV-specific synthesis only where relevant subgroup findings can be identified separately.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Their use will be documented transparently.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Although NK cells contribute to antiviral immunity, immune regulation, and tumor surveillance, findings concerning their circulating frequency, phenotypic characteristics, and functional responses remain heterogeneous.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The anticipated outcome is an evidence map identifying the distribution of research across HBV-related clinical conditions, the extent to which NK-cell quantity, phenotype, and function have been examined, major sources of methodological heterogeneity, and areas where evidence is limited or insufficiently comparable.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review aims to systematically map and critically examine the available evidence on the quantity, phenotype, and function of peripheral blood natural killer (NK) cells across the clinical spectrum of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including chronic HBV infection and hepatitis, HBV-related liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, and HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Differences in clinical populations, disease classification, antiviral treatment, blood sample processing, flow cytometric gating strategies, measurement denominators, and functional assay conditions may limit direct comparisons between studies. The review will be guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), with additional attention to transparent reporting of literature searches using PRISMA-S. Studies involving mixed HCC etiologies will be considered for HBV-specific synthesis only where relevant subgroup findings can be identified separately. Their use will be documented transparently. Although NK cells contribute to antiviral immunity, immune regulation, and tumor surveillance, findings concerning their circulating frequency, phenotypic characteristics, and functional responses remain heterogeneous. The anticipated outcome is an evidence map identifying the distribution of research across HBV-related clinical conditions, the extent to which NK-cell quantity, phenotype, and function have been examined, major sources of methodological heterogeneity, and areas where evidence is limited or insufficiently comparable.

title: Interferon therapy reduces incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with high risk of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the clear comparison between IFN and NAs groups and the statistically significant results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of interferon (IFN) therapy versus nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC. A retrospective cohort study enrolled 368 patients, with 120 receiving IFN therapy and 248 receiving NA therapy alone. After 5 years, HCC incidence was 2.54% in the IFN group and 25.74% in the NAs group (P < 0.001). title: Interpretability-driven feature engineering enables compact and accurate multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: Clinical artificial intelligence (AI) often trades predictive performance against interpretability. This study develops an interpretability-driven feature engineering framework for multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 36,024 hospitalization records from 22,001 patients were included. The framework integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based main and interaction effects was used to construct compact machine learning models for classifying disease non-progression, liver cirrhosis (LC), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.methods: SHAP main effects selected the top 15 features per outcome; TreeSHAP interactions selected four pairwise terms.
analysis.main_results: The full-feature models achieved superior discrimination (AUCs: 0.927, 0.897, and 0.899) for classifying hospitalization-recorded disease non-progression, LC, and HCC, respectively. The corresponding compact models maintained strong discrimination (AUCs: 0.911, 0.882, and 0.890) with 80.8% fewer features. Interaction models yielded subtle AUC shifts (AUCs: 0.912, 0.881, and 0.891) while characterizing potential clinical joint-effect patterns.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C are infectious diseases that can be transmitted from pregnant women to their babies during pregnancy, childbirth, or after birth. Screening examinations in pregnant women are important as an early detection effort to prevent vertical transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study employed a descriptive research design. The research was conducted at the Laboratory of the Sidoarjo Community Health Center from January to February 2026, involving 40 pregnant women who attended antenatal care (ANC) examinations.
analysis.methods: Testing was performed using the rapid immunochromatographic method on blood samples collected from the respondents to detect HBsAb and Anti-HCV antibodies.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that, based on age, most respondents were in the 20–35 years age group, accounting for 32 individuals (80%). Based on gestational age, the majority of respondents were in the first trimester, totaling 22 individuals (55%). The HBsAb examination results indicated that 38 respondents (95%) were non-reactive and 2 respondents (5%) were reactive. Meanwhile, the Anti-HCV examination results showed that all 40 respondents (100%) were non-reactive.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides a profile of antibody test results for Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C among pregnant women using the immunochromatographic method, highlighting the prevalence of non-reactive results for both.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: It is important for pregnant women to undergo Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C screening as a preventive measure to reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report on the limitations of the study or the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the profile of Hepatitis B antibody (HBsAb) and Hepatitis C antibody (Anti-HCV) test results among pregnant women using the immunochromatographic method at the Sidoarjo Community Health Center. The research was conducted between January and February 2026, involving 40 pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) examinations. Testing was performed using rapid immunochromatographic methods on blood samples to detect HBsAb and Anti-HCV antibodies. The results indicated that 80% of the participants were aged 20–35 years, with 55% in the first trimester. For HBsAb, 95% of the participants were non-reactive, while 5% were reactive. All 40 participants were non-reactive for Anti-HCV. The findings emphasize the importance of screening for Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C in pregnant women to prevent vertical transmission. The study is descriptive and provides a snapshot of antibody profiles in this population, but it does not report on limitations or the strength of the evidence.
